clue.text: Actor in rep, really excited to land lead in Othello

indicators.note: to land something is to take it in, so the leading letter is drawn into the jumbled letters
excited letters are stirred up and jump about, so rep and really are jumbled together
the lead in a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A repertory actor gets thrilled at being cast as Othello, the lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges REP and REALLY; 'to land' takes in O, the 'lead in' Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone who takes a part in a play or scenario is a performer of a role, so an actor fits.

clue.text: Slice top off beef that's ready for eating

indicators.note: slicing the top off a down entry removes its first letter

parts.note: to beef is to complain, as is to gripe

explanation.surface: A cook trims a joint of beef that is ready to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like the meat but is the verb meaning complain; 'Slice top off' removes the G.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or cheese at its best for eating is described as mature, the usual synonym.

clue.text: Woman working with men in the field

indicators.note: in places the working men inside the word for the field

parts.note: a lea is a grassy field or meadow
a machine that is on is working
OR, other ranks, is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A woman labours alongside the farmhands out in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: OR stands for 'other ranks', a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers or men.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female given name, so it can stand for any woman in crossword convention.

clue.text: Intend taking action to make newspapers cover costs

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first part sits on top of the second and so covers it

parts.note: the press is the collective term for newspapers
charges are prices or costs demanded

explanation.surface: Someone threatens a lawsuit to force the newspapers to pay their legal costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' looks like paying the costs, but it places one part above the other in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To formally accuse someone is the step that starts a criminal prosecution, so it signals the intent to take legal action.

clue.text: A street light not where it should be?

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A streetlamp seems to have been put in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone off course or misplaced is wandering from its proper position.

clue.text: Senior manager departs after Aussie truck's delivered

indicators.note: after places the departure letter behind the truck

parts.note: an exec is an executive, a senior manager
ute, short for utility vehicle, is the Australian word for a pickup truck
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A boss leaves once the Australian lorry has made its drop-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' looks like the truck's cargo but means carried out, as a plan or a performance is.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform or carry out a plan or a speech is to bring it off, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Rubbish dumped in skip is humming

indicators.note: the letters sit dumped inside the phrase skip is humming, spanning its words

explanation.surface: Refuse tipped into a skip has started to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' is British slang for smelling bad; a skip is a large open bin for building waste.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old exclamation of contempt meaning nonsense, as rubbish can be used.

clue.text: Poet, first to describe the three wise men

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: 1st, written IST, is the abbreviation for first
the Magi are the three wise men of the nativity story

explanation.surface: A poet is the first to write about the wise men of the nativity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describe' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round something.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagism was an early 20th-century school of poets such as Pound, so a member of it is a writer of verse.

clue.text: Stirring up the dragon's quite rash

indicators.note: stirring up mixes things around, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Poking a sleeping dragon is a reckless move.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilful, impetuous person acts without caution, which is being reckless.

clue.text: Having premises really owned by brewery?

parts.note: proper is colloquial British for really or thoroughly, as in proper good
a tied house is a pub owned by a brewery and bound to sell its beer

explanation.surface: A pub chain whose premises are actually owned by a brewery.
explanation.walkthrough: A British 'tied' pub must sell only its owning brewery's beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owns land or buildings is landed, possessing real estate.

clue.text: Priest's first to leave after mass, actually

indicators.note: first here applies to each of the following four words in turn, taking its opening letter

explanation.surface: After the service, the priest really is the first to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; only leave, after, mass and actually give their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tibetan Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher holds the title, so it is a kind of priest.

clue.text: Listened as part of roof fell in?

parts.note: the eaves are the overhanging lower edge of a roof
to have dropped is to have fallen down

explanation.surface: Someone listened as a bit of the roof collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: The image of eavesdroppers once standing under the eaves to overhear gives the second reading its point.
explanation.definitionFit: Secretly overhearing a private conversation is a form of listening in.

clue.text: Perhaps they have large sign with "No criminals allowed" on the front

definitions.text: Perhaps they have large sign with "No criminals allowed" on the front

indicators.note: on the front places the barred criminals before the rest

parts.note: cons are convicts, criminals
tabu, a variant of taboo, means forbidden, a no
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Police forces might put up a big notice banning criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' is a zodiac sign; 'No criminals' gives CONS and TABU in the reverse order, set at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Police forces would perhaps keep out lawbreakers, so the whole clue hints at their name.

clue.text: With time, see apprentice heading off … to become this?

definitions.text: With time, see apprentice heading off … to become this?

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: the apprentice word loses its heading, its first letter

parts.note: a learner is a trainee or apprentice

explanation.surface: Give a trainee time and they will end up on the payroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link inviting the reader to watch; the dots lead to the whole-clue reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice in time graduates to being a salaried worker, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Brave fellow chasing a crowd out of the King's Head

indicators.note: chasing puts the fellow behind the rest
out of means the king's initial is removed from the crowd word

parts.note: a pack is a crowd or mob

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: he is a male, a fellow

explanation.surface: A brave man pursues a mob from a pub called the King's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name; 'Brave' is a noun, a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior of the Native American people is called a brave, a dated noun.

clue.text: Father's words encouraging acquisitiveness

definitions.meaning: one who sires a child, the father
split in two, the letters read as advice to be someone who acquires things

explanation.definitionFit: To beget is to father a child, so one who does so is the sire or parent.

clue.text: Word of warning about ex-wife's shock treatment?

indicators.note: about means the warning word goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: cave, Latin for beware, was schoolboy slang shouted as a warning
old can mean former, as ex does

explanation.surface: A man's warning about his former wife's jolting behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is a shock of hair: this is a chemical perm, not a jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent wave set with chemicals rather than heat is a hair treatment, and a shock is a mass of hair.

clue.text: French delicacy? Load tons onto backs of some lorries

indicators.note: onto puts the load after the lorries' back letters
the backs of words are their final letters

parts.note: a cargo is a load carried

explanation.surface: Heavy freight is being loaded onto the back of a few trucks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked in garlic butter are a famous dish of French cuisine, hence a delicacy from France.

clue.text: Name-dropping colleague at party somewhere in S London

indicators.note: in a down entry dropping sends a letter lower, here to the bottom

parts.note: a crony is a close companion or colleague
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A show-off workmate lets slip famous names at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' reads as the social habit but moves N to the end. Croydon is a borough in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large town and borough on the southern edge of London, so an example of a place there.

clue.text: Science master is overshadowed by English teacher

indicators.note: a thing overshadowed by another is covered by it, so the teacher wraps round the small word

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A science teacher feels eclipsed by a colleague in the English department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' looks like a schoolteacher, but here means a great expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, inventor of the light bulb and phonograph, was a towering figure in applied science.

clue.text: Composer who made his mark?

parts.note: John ... was a Victorian English church composer, and one who leaves a mark or blot is literally a ...

explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer, organist and composer of The Crucifixion, shares his name with someone who leaves a mark.

clue.text: Soldier making request to have change of air

parts.note: to ask is to make a request

indicators.note: a change of the word air means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier asks permission to get some fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the term for an East African native soldier serving in a colonial army, so a soldier.

clue.text: East Poland is so amazingly accessible

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something astonishingly altered, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A travel pitch boasting how easy it is to reach eastern Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available for a person to use whenever they wish is within reach, an idiom for accessible.

clue.text: Realise addict is wanting ecstasy -

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the drug letter goes missing

parts.note: a fiend is an addict or fanatic, as in a dope fiend
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone comes to see that a drug user is craving a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like craving but means lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover or come to know something is to realise it, as in finding it true.

clue.text: Who's regularly sporting no undies?

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of no undies, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about who habitually goes without underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A person wearing no clothes at all is certainly going without underwear, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Ancient city west of mountains cut off during terrible raid

indicators.note: during places the compass point and mountain word within the jumbled raid
terrible signals that the letters of raid are thrown into disorder
cut off removes the final letter of the mountain word

parts.note: alpine means relating to high mountains

explanation.definitionFit: This Pakistani city stands on a site settled since antiquity, so it is an old city.

clue.text: Phone doctor about onset of neuralgia

parts.note: to doctor is to tamper with or rig

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Calling the GP about early nerve pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, to falsify, not a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is British usage for calling them on the telephone.

clue.text: Interrupted by man of wit, appear embarrassed and confused

indicators.note: a phrase interrupted by something has it inserted into its middle

parts.note: to be red is to look flushed with embarrassment
Oscar Wilde was famed for his wit

explanation.surface: Someone cut off by a sharp wit looks flustered and muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being baffled or perplexed is a state of mental disorder, a synonym of muddled.
